summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a DHCP relay between two isolated L2 segments — eth1 (192.168.10.0/24, toward node2) and eth2 (192.168.20.0/24, toward node3) — using the platform's own docker-dhcp-relay image invoked directly (dhcrelay -i eth2 -i eth1 192.168.10.2), persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d for the IPs and docker restart-policy=unless-stopped for the relay container. Installed and configured isc-dhcp-server (package "dhcp") on node2, binding to eth1 with subnet declarations for both the local segment and node3's subnet (192.168.20.0/24, range .100-.200). Diagnosed and fixed a routing gap where node2's DHCPOFFER (destined to node1's giaddr 192.168.20.1) had no route and fell through the default gateway; added a static route via node1's eth1. Verified node3 obtains a real DHCP lease (192.168.20.100/24) from node2's service through node1's relay via NetworkManager. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, capturing pre/post boot_id changes and confirming the DHCP-relay path, lease data, and SONiC container stack fully recovered after each reboot (node3 automatically re-obtained its lease after its own reboot).
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (SONiC) has eth1 facing node2's segment and eth2 facing node3's segment, both otherwise isolated L2 domains
Assigned static IPs 192.168.10.1/24 (eth1) and 192.168.20.1/24 (eth2) on node1, persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/dhcp-relay-links
Assigned static IP 192.168.10.2/24 on node2 eth1 via nmcli (persistent NM connection)
Added CentOS7 vault repo on node2 and installed dhcp (isc-dhcp-server) and tcpdump packages

Configured /etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf on node2 with subnet declarations for 192.168.10.0/24 (local) and 192.168.20.0/24 (node3's subnet, range .100-.200), started/enabled dhcpd, opened firewalld dhcp service

Launched isc-dhcp-relay's dhcrelay binary on node1 via docker run --network host --entrypoint /usr/sbin/dhcrelay against docker-dhcp-relay image, relaying between eth2 and eth1 to server 192.168.10.2; set container restart policy to unless-stopped

Diagnosed via tcpdump on node1/node2 interfaces that DHCPOFFER packets from node2 were not reaching node1 because node2 lacked a route to 192.168.20.1 (the giaddr); fixed by adding a static route (192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.1) on node2's eth1 connection
Configured node3 eth1 as NetworkManager DHCP client and verified it obtains address 192.168.20.100/24 end-to-end through the relay
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service/IP/lease state) on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via native reboot, polled each until exec access returned, and verified boot_id changed on each

Verified post-restart recovery: node1's eth1/eth2 IPs and dhcrelay container came back automatically; node2's dhcpd, eth1 IP, static route, and lease file persisted; node3 automatically re-acquired its 192.168.20.100/24 DHCP lease via the relay after its own reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 obtains its address from node2's DHCP service despite being on a different L2 segment of node1
evidence.summary: node3's dhclient/NetworkManager successfully completes DHCPDISCOVER/OFFER/REQUEST/ACK and binds to 192.168.20.100/24; node2's dhcpd.leases file shows the corresponding active lease for node3's MAC

evidence.requirement: DHCP relay path correctness (root cause diagnosis and fix)
evidence.summary: tcpdump showed DHCPDISCOVER correctly relayed node1 eth2->eth1->node2, but DHCPOFFER never left node2's eth1 until a static route to node1's giaddr (192.168.20.1) was added on node2

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 34192023...; reboot acknowledged; polled until boot_id changed to d022c1ec... confirming restart; eth1/eth2 IPs and dhcrelay container auto-recovered, all 10 SONiC containers back, and a fresh end-to-end DHCP renewal from node3 succeeded post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2fc81aed...; reboot acknowledged; polled until boot_id changed to 02a1de53... confirming restart; dhcpd active, eth1 static IP and route to 192.168.20.0/24 persisted, and prior lease data intact in dhcpd.leases

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 738d0aac...; reboot acknowledged; polled until boot_id changed to 4cf008a6... confirming restart; NetworkManager automatically re-obtained the 192.168.20.100/24 DHCP lease via the relay after reboot, proving end-to-end recovery
